chunks: 5 - He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Za'farani reported to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, who said: Lut ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Jundab narrated to me, from his father, who said:

When the allegiance was pledged to Uthman, I heard al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, may Allah have mercy on him, saying to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: By God, O Abd al-Rahman, I have never seen the like of what has been done to the people of this House after their Prophet, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family and grant them peace.

So Abd al-Rahman said to him: And what concern is that of yours, O Miqdad?! He said: Indeed, by God, I love them because of the love of the Messenger of Allah for them, and there overcomes me, by God, a grief that I cannot express at all, because of Quraysh's claim of superiority over the people through their noble lineage and their uniting to strip the authority of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family and grant them peace, from their hands.

So Abd al-Rahman said to him: Woe to you! By God, I have exerted myself for your sake! So al-Miqdad said to him: Indeed, by God, you have left a man who is among those who enjoin the truth and through it act with justice. Indeed, by God, if I had supporters against Quraysh, I would have fought them as I fought them on the day of Badr and Uhud.
So Abd al-Rahman said to him: May your mother be bereaved of you, O Miqdad! Let not the people hear this speech from you! Indeed, by God, I fear that you will be the cause of division and sedition.

Jundab said: So I came to him after he had left his place, and I said to him: O Miqdad, I am among your supporters! He said: May Allah have mercy on you, for what we seek cannot be achieved by two or three men. So I left him and went in to Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and I mentioned to him what he had said and what I had said. He said: So he prayed for us for goodness.

key_terms.أَهْلِ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: Ahlulbayt (the People of this House), referring to the Prophet's family
key_terms.بُويِعَ: Bay'ah (pledge of allegiance), the formal oath of fealty given to a new caliph
key_terms.سُلْطَانِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The authority of the Messenger of Allah, his divinely-mandated political succession
key_terms.فُرْقَةٍ وَفِتْنَةٍ: Division and sedition, the feared consequence of public dissent
key_terms.يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُون: Those who enjoin truth and through it act justly, an echo of Quran 7:181

ai.seo_question: What did al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad say to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf after Uthman's bay'ah about the rights of Ahlulbayt?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the companion al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi's protest to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf after the bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) was given to Uthman. Al-Miqdad expresses his grief at the injustice done to the Prophet's Household (Ahlulbayt), declaring his love for them on account of the Prophet's love for them. He accuses Quraysh of claiming superiority over the people while collectively stripping the authority that the Messenger of Allah had designated. When Jundab offers his support, al-Miqdad replies that what they seek requires far more than two or three men. Jundab then visits Imam Ali and reports the exchange, and Ali prays for them with goodness.
